acceptanceCriteria: Every configured host type has a context-warning delivery path; none reports UNSUPPORTED when the host config declares the host-neutral path (test)
`dispatch salvage --attempt A` writes the secret-screened handoff note for a running or externally stopped attempt (test)
`launched` and `stopped` events record whether warnings and salvage ran (test)
ATR requirements added with traces; focused dispatch tests pass
body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#1148 (owner, 2026-10-18). In-session context warnings and hard-stop salvage work for only one host type; other hosts (for example a run/CLI wrapper) report contextDelivery UNSUPPORTED. Salvage runs only on a native hard stop, so a program-side supervisor that stops a session earlier gets no handoff note. Ask: (1) a host-neutral delivery path declared in host config (for example a polled file, or a stdin/notification hook); (2) `dispatch salvage --attempt A` that a supervisor can trigger on demand. Related: V1-1768 (opencode plugin, no-tool-call sessions, candidate hand-off notes) and V1-1792 (line-based salvage screening). Add requirements in ATR.
title: dispatch: host-neutral context-warning delivery and an on-demand salvage command (GitHub #1148)
